alex: Quick sync — discovered two KV OOMs on canary last night during a sustained burst. Continuous batching appears to be admitting batches that push the live KV footprint past the slot limit. Can people scan the profile and propose an OOM-avoidance heuristic? :thinking:

perf-bot: (auto) 3932100522 trace uploaded. Peak device mem + KV growth correlated with batch admissions between 23:12-23:40 UTC. Kernel: matmul-fp32-tiling shows +12% memory vs quantized.

maya: Can you paste the trace IDs and a snippet of the KV usage timeline? Curious if it's steady growth or step jumps per request.

alex: Trace IDs: trace/3932100522 and trace/3932100580. Snip from timeline:
`kv_used_mb = [812, 814, 820, 842, 890, 950]`
We saw a sudden delta when a 6k-token batch landed — projected_add ~ 140MB based on avg_kv_per_token.

jun: Noted — kernel selection changed mid-run to the FP32 tiling kernel for sequences > 4k (fallback from quantized). That kernel has larger transient allocations for prefetched keys. So two factors: batch size + kernel memory profile.

samir: Thinking heuristic: make batch admission aware of current KV occupancy. If kv_used / kv_limit > threshold then scale *token_budget* down. Keeps batching but prevents big jumps.

lisa: Agreed. Also need projection math: projected_kv_add = avg_kv_per_token * requested_tokens. If kv_used + projected_kv_add > kv_limit * headroom_threshold => either trim tokens or reject. But consider fairness for long-context users.

alex: Proposed pseudo: 
```
headroom = kv_limit * 0.85
projected_add = avg_kv_per_token(model, user) * batch_tokens
if kv_used + projected_add > headroom:
  allowed_tokens = max(min_tokens, floor((headroom - kv_used)/avg_kv_per_token))
  if allowed_tokens < min_tokens: reject_batch() else trim_batch(allowed_tokens)
else:
  admit_batch()
```

maya: Trimming might be surprising UX; we should prefer soft-admit: accept but mark for background compaction or mark lower priority, then evict cold keys proactively. Also add SLA-aware prioritization (SRE, paid tiers).

jun: Background compaction is promising. We prototyped an LRU-like compaction that aggressively drops >N-long tail entries for models that have large KV fragmentation. It reduces footprint by ~8-12% without affecting quality in our eval set.

samir: We tried a different approach in experiments: token_budget_multiplier = clamp(1 - kv_occupancy_ratio, 0.5, 1.0). On canary this reduced OOMs by 25% but slightly increased per-request latency due to smaller batching efficiency.

alex: Experiment results: canary with multiplier 0.6 (for kv_occupancy_ratio~0.4) => OOMs down from 12 to 3 in 24h window, 95p latency +5ms, cost +2%. Tradeoff seems acceptable for safety.

perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/3932100522 (95p mem, 99p latency graphs attached in trace).

lisa: For rollout config I propose: 
`token_budget_multiplier = max(0.5, 1 - kv_occupancy_ratio * 1.2)`
plus a hard floor `min_batch_tokens = 8` to avoid kernel overhead for very small batches.

maya: I'll run the canary with 1% traffic for 3 hours, then bump to 5% if no OOMs. Will add an alert on kv_used change and 95p device mem. @alex want me to include background compaction toggle?

alex: Yes include compaction toggle off by default, enable in a second canary if initial pass looks stable. Start with 1% -> 3h -> 5%. Document rollback signal: any >=2 OOMs in 1h.

jun: Caveat: small batch multiplier hurts quantized throughput due to lower kernel occupancy — add min_batch_tokens and route tiny batches to the low-latency kernel variant. Kernel-routing + batch-pacer combo should amortize overhead.

samir: Also consider a fast path: if model quantized variant available, and kv_occupancy high, prefer quantized kernel to reduce transient mem even if marginally slower.

alex: Good calls. I'll open a config PR with: batch_pacer (kv_headroom=0.85, min_tokens=8, token_multiplier_expr as lisa suggested), kernel_routing rules for small batches, and a compaction feature flag.

maya: +1. I'll queue the canary and add a dashboard panel showing kv_occupancy_ratio, avg_kv_per_token, admitted_tokens distribution.

jun: One more note — add telemetry for `projected_kv_conflict` per admission (boolean) so we can aggregate how often we trimmed vs rejected vs accepted.

alex: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll sync the PR and tag eng-runtime for review. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: (auto) follow-up: created issue INF-5329 to track rollout, experiments, and canary results.
